title: molt new-user --from <dir>: scaffold a user stack from a template other than Molt's skeleton, by the same code and tokens
body:
`molt new-user` scaffolds a user stack only from Molt's own skeleton, `templates/molt-user`, a fixed path in `molt_new_user` (`lib/newuser.sh`) with no option for another template. hv's bootcamp gives each participant their own `Molt-<login>`, scaffolded at first run from a course template in the image (hv's ruling, 5 Nov, through pipeliner-sc). That template cannot go through new-user today, so a first-run script would need a second scaffolder of its own, which could drift from Molt's.

hv chose option (a) of molt-vc's answer to pipeliner-sc (`/Users/matts/Devel/scratch/molt-vc/answer-pipeliner-sc-2026-11-05.md`, its addendum), and allocated it in molt-vc's window on 5 Nov.

The change:
- `--from <dir>` names the template new-user scaffolds from. Without it, new-user uses Molt's own skeleton, as now.
- The template goes through the same code: the same `__MOLT_*__` tokens are substituted in file contents and path names, so Molt keeps one scaffolder. No `.git` directory is copied from the template.
- new-user refuses a `--from` that is not a directory, or that holds no `config/`, since a stack is found by its `config/`. Each refusal names the path and why, and nothing is written.
- Every value can come from flags, so a first-run script never meets a prompt.
- The next steps new-user prints keep the resleeve, `git init` and the first commit for any template. The GitHub remote lines stay for Molt's own skeleton only.

Size S.
